featured_reviews.name: Sagar Mungekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Deeply mourned with the sad demise of my stray
One month ago I had sent a post wherein I posted how IDA saved my stray dog, but today I am posting again as the dog died on Sunday afternoon 4/06/23, Some issues I felt are important to share so posting, After bringing back the dog fell ill within 15 days.This time her hemoglobin was only 1, I medicated her as directed by the doctors at my home then also the levels dropped, so after a week I admitted her again, I was charged 2000/- for it even though I paid 3500/- in first instance.  Saving the dog was more imp than amount so I paid without any complaint or issue, again after 15 days she got discharged the doctors said that she is keeping good health and her haemoglobin level have gone to 8, seeing her health I was not convinced but the doctor insisted saying you can't keep as she is better now, if they would have kept for 4-5 days more she could have definitely recovered properly but the doctor denied to keep. One consulting doctor comes on 3 days on Tues, wed & Thursday but he said to take her back on Monday itself so i had to discharge her. From Wednesday she stopped to eat at all so i called up in IDA emergency services number, But they directed me to samast Mahajan but things did not work from them too, I tried to contact the visiting doctor, but in vain I feel if just if she could direct me on phone itself things would have worked but it didn't happen.
If at all IDA authorities see this message I would request that please do not discharge any pet or stray till it gets really well because we are ignorant about how to deal with the situation. I strongly feel that the doctors in hospital should be more responsible as for us and for strays you are next to god so please take care, please don't ignore animals saying they are trying to run away or they come to bite as this is expected from pets/ strays without doubt, also as the fortification is too strong so they can't run away , as well as the ground staff under them is good so they get good support from them, the people in management or the trustees should look into this issues more strictly as it is matter of life or survival of those animals who can't talk & are totally dependent.
Again with joined hands Irequest all the pet lovers please ensure that the pet or stray is completely well before discharging him/ her. IDA authorities also please consider my request & take my post positively I have lost my dog but it may be of help for others. IDA has the ability to strive for animal welfare so please please dont miss this god gif To maintain that they have to be at mark, the doctors are the saviours & they must act accordingly. Somewhat bad  & disappointing experience this time, sorry to say.

featured_reviews.name: sahil khullar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I rescued a tiny kitten from Sea Link and took care of it for three days, and that alone made me realize how incredibly tough kitten care actually is, especially for someone like me who has only ever had a dog. I was confused and didn’t know what to do next. After checking shelters and all possible options, I came across Anuja ma’am’s page, Meow Love, and decided to call her.

She sounded very sweet on the phone, but in person I realized she is actually quite strict, and honestly that made me trust her even more. She is very upfront about everything, including her charges, and extremely particular about where the kitten goes. For her this is not a joke, it is about a life. She vets adopters properly, checks whether the home is suitable, and will not just hand a kitten to anyone. That gave me huge peace of mind.

She got my kitten adopted in just one month to a family that had already adopted from her before, so he now has a friend as well, which makes me so happy. It depends from kitten to kitten, but both he and I were extremely lucky that she found him a home so quickly.

Her services may seem pricey at first but they are similar to others offering similar services, but considering the effort, care, and the kind of homes she finds, it was 100% worth it to me. As a rescuer, you either invest your own time or you entrust that responsibility to someone like her, and if you can afford it, I would strongly recommend it.

Anyone looking to adopt from her is extremely lucky. The way she cares for kittens is something most people simply cannot match. Just look at her own cats, they are some of the biggest, healthiest, most beautiful cats I have ever seen. You can be absolutely sure your kitten was in the best hands before coming home to you.

Please don’t be put off by her directness. She simply cares more about cats than about pleasing people. Please, please consider adopting from her. It may genuinely be one of the best decisions you can make.

featured_reviews.name: Nisha Verma
featured_reviews.review_text:
She was extremely rude and did not have basic manners about how to speak with customers.
I informed her that I have two Persian cats who are well-mannered and well-trained, and that I was looking for boarding. She asked a few questions regarding boarding, such as whether they are litter-trained and about their nature. As a responsible pet parent, I then asked some general questions from my side—like whether the cats are kept in cages or at home. She said they don’t keep cats in cages.
However, when I asked whether Indian and Persian breed cats are kept together, she suddenly started shouting and was not ready to listen to my concern. Instead of explaining how they manage different breeds, she became defensive and accused me of being partial. She even said that only she understands pets and that I don’t care about my own pets, which was very hurtful and completely untrue.
My concern was purely based on experience. Sometimes Indian and Persian cats can fight, and I have personally seen an Indian cat attack a Persian cat very badly. Out of concern for my pets’ safety, I asked this question. Instead of calmly explaining their handling process, she kept shouting, blamed me, and forced her own assumptions on me without listening.
She also brought up irrelevant topics like age difference and spoke in a very bossy manner. At one point, she directly said, “Do you want to fight or what?” which is highly unprofessional.
For the record, I love all animals. I even take care of Indie kittens from the street whenever I find them. This was never about discrimination—it was about understanding how dominating behavior between different cats is managed.
In my opinion, a true animal lover understands that every pet has a different nature and behavior. It’s not about comparing animals, but about knowing how to handle them properly. If she were a true pet lover, she should have understood my concern and explained how they manage cats with dominating tendencies instead of reacting aggressively.
Most importantly, she seriously needs to learn how to talk to customers. She is very rude, bossy, and a poor listener.
